MK: Mrs. Jung does qualify for NH level of care (currently has 3 ADL needs)
SBP: Home-based primary care with homemaker/home health aides: This could be a good/feasible option for Mrs. Jung.
She would be able to stay in the home with her daughter as she desires

Appointments could be coordinated through a home-based primary care program (typically able to accommodate more of what the patient’s scheduling needs are) and reduce the amount of time the daughter would need to take her to appointments
Her Medicare insurance would cover the usual costs of the provider visits
Home-based primary care team could help her get set up with county-based home health aide services if she qualifies for through Medicaid
Home-based primary care social worker could also help with utilizing private pay resources for daytime private home health aides
Daughter might feel less stressed knowing her mom was receiving assistance at home
Homemaker/home health aides cannot always cover all the hours needed by a family and might be inconsistent
Home-based primary care with home health aides would not necessarily help the social isolation that Mrs. Jung may be experiencing
Private pay home health aides are expensive
PACE: This could also be a good/feasible option for Mrs. Jung.
PACE could provide a NH level of care while keeping Mrs. Jung in her home with her daughter as she desires
PACE day programs can compensate for the hours her daughter is at work; her daughter could continue to assist her in the home during the evening hours
PACE day programs could help Mrs. Jung get out of the home (provided she felt safe to do so), provide transportation, meals, and assistance with her showering/dressing at the PACE program
At PACE, Mrs. Jung can see her doctor and interprofessional care team members all in one place
PACE’s comprehensive services may reduce the daughter’s caregiver burden
PACE would assist with socialization and hopefully engage Mrs. Jung in a community of peers through the day program
Mrs. Jung might not want to leave her home to attend PACE, or change her PCP to the PACE physician

Mrs. Jung would be able to utilize her Medicare benefit, but we would need to find out if she qualifies for Medicaid as well (left ambiguous in the case) to determine if all the PACE costs could be paid for without out of pocket expense
RCFE (Assisted Living or Adult Group Home): This would not be the best option for Mrs. Jung.
RCFE would provide her with meals, housekeeping
RCFE could manage her medications and provide her with dressing and shower assistance (for a fee)
RCFE could provide socialization with peers
Daughter’s caregiver burden may be reduced
Mrs. Jung doesn’t want to leave her home and has an alternative (her daughter who could care for her during the evening hours with additional daytime assistance)
Mrs. Jung’s care needs (ADL assistance, medication management) would cost a significant amount of “extras” on top of an RCFE’s room and board costs

Mrs. Jung has an intentionally ambiguous financial situation, though could potentially sell the home she owns (and unfortunately also then need to evict her daughter) to be able to pay for RCFE level of care
NH: This would not be the best option for Mrs. Jung though possible.
NH could manage all her ADL needs, monitor for and help assess falls
NH could provide socialization with peers
Ambiguous Medicaid status; if she has Medicaid, will need to find a facility that accepts Medicaid
If she does not currently have Medicaid, there is usually a lengthy application process followed by a search for a SNF that would accommodate a long-term care patient on Medicaid
If not qualifying for Medicaid, Mrs. Jung would need to pay out of pocket for her nursing home room (expensive!)
